final_answer:
The Meridian Tidal Pilot's sole major failure occurred when **Turbine T-4** went offline on 14 March 2025 after its **bearing seal corroded through**, allowing seawater into the nacelle — the only failure causing a multi-week outage, with root cause traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing.

Over 24 months the pilot delivered **18.7 GWh** to the grid, **6% below** the 19.9 GWh forecast. The project cost reached **EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million**, a **12.4% overrun** (EUR 4.55 million) driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

Environmentally, independent fish monitoring found **no statistically significant change** in fish migration counts before and after installation (p = 0.41).

Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing titanium fasteners with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles, a change accepted in principle by the steering group.

The steering group **approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026**, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
